LOW FINDING 1 (IsSequenceRaceException misattribution on the DbUpdateConcurrencyException branch) - FIXED in OfficialNumberService.cs. Rewrote the expression body so exception.Entries.Any(e => ReferenceEquals(e.Entity, row)) gates BOTH branches (DbUpdateConcurrencyException and the SQLite PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE branch), exactly as the finding's suggested fix specified. Updated the XML doc on IsSequenceRaceException and the inline comment in IssueCoreAsync to describe both branches being narrowed the same way (previously the doc only described the SQLite branch as narrowed).

LOW FINDING 2 (Detached-recovery branch untested) - FIXED with a new test, Issue_WhenTheConflictingRowVanishesBeforeTheReload_DetachesTheStaleAddedEntry_AndTheRetrySucceeds. Since a live two-connection race cannot deterministically reach "the row that just raced is gone again by the time of ReloadAsync" (SQLite/WAL turns real overlap into a busy error, as the existing INSERT-race test's own comment documents), this test uses a test-only EF Core SaveChangesInterceptor (DeleteRowOnFirstSaveFailureInterceptor, nested private class in the test file) that deletes the just-raced (kind,year) row through the SAME WakeelDb/connection/transaction the failing SaveChanges is using, the instant that SaveChanges fails (ISaveChangesInterceptor.SaveChangesFailedAsync) -- before the service's own catch block calls ReloadAsync. This relies on EF Core rolling back the failed SaveChanges to its internal savepoint before dispatching SaveChangesFailedAsync, so the interceptor's delete lands in the still-open outer (caller-owned) transaction rather than being undone with the failed insert; verified empirically (not just by inspection) that this produces a genuine PRIMARY KEY violation on attempt 1, a real "reload finds nothing" on attempt 2, and a successful sequence-1 result. Verified by hand: removing the detach branch's `if (db.Entry(row).State == EntityState.Added) { db.Entry(row).State = EntityState.Detached; }` from OfficialNumberService.cs now makes this new test FAIL with the exact untranslated EF identity-conflict InvalidOperationException the branch exists to prevent ("The instance of entity type OfficialNumber cannot be tracked because another instance with the same key... is already being tracked") -- confirmed via a real dotnet test run, then the branch was restored.

All three review findings were verified end-to-end by actually breaking the corresponding production code, confirming the updated/new tests fail for the right reason, then restoring the fix and confirming the full suite (174/174) is green again.
